title_en: 'I Hope We Will Survive' — Denis Villeneuve Was 'Deeply Disappointed' by Disney's Decision to Release Avengers: Doomsday on the Same Day as Dune: Part Three
summary_en: Denis Villeneuve has revealed his disappointment at Disney's decision to release Avengers: Doomsday in theaters on the same day as Dune: Part Three.
body_en:
Denis Villeneuve has revealed his disappointment at Disney's decision to release Avengers: Doomsday in theaters on the same day as Dune: Part Three .
Doomsday was initially due out on May 1 this year, but was delayed to December 18 — a date Dune 3 had already claimed. Because of the clash, Avengers: Doomsday misses out on an Imax release, with Villeneuve’s trilogy-ender having already snapped up exclusivity for the big screens.
In a new interview with Time , Villeneuve ran through the various release challenges the Dune movies have endured, and said he thought that with Part Three, he’d finally have a clear run of it.
“Listen, I will be honest,” he began. “The first Dune came out at the end of the pandemic. We made a great box office in a very rough environment. But we had the winds against us. Then the second movie, same thing. We were meant to release in the fall, and we had to release at the end of winter because of the two Hollywood strikes. We had success, but it was not easy. The third time, I said to myself, ‘Finally, there is no pandemic, no strike in sight. We will have a normal release.’ Then Disney put the biggest franchise of all time against us. I’m no fool. Those movies are a mammoth.
“So I was deeply disappointed. But we had committed to this date, to Imax. It was impossible to move. So I accepted my fate, praying to the gods of cinema. Dune is not a mammoth like the Avengers, but it’s a sexy little animal that has a lot of firepower, and I hope we will survive. It could be one of the biggest box-office weekends of all time because of both movies. Am I in competition with the Avengers? Absolutely not. It’s a T. rex. But I stand proud because I think the film delivers.”
Avengers: Doomsday is expected to be one of the biggest movies of all time, with a box office haul Disney will hope matches up to previous Avengers films. It’s thought December 18 could be the largest box office weekend ever, when you factor in Dune 3’s launch. Fans have dubbed the dual release ‘DunesDay,’ in a sort of sci-fi heavy follow-up to 'Barbenheimer.'
But will Dune 3 benefit from Avengers: Doomsday’s release or suffer from it? Villeneuve is putting a brave face on the situation here — I wouldn’t be surprised if there’s plenty of worry internally.
According to the New York Times , Legendary Entertainment and Warner Bros. spent an estimated $200 million to make Dune 3, excluding marketing. The publication suggests the two movies could cannibalize each other, with Disney pushing its new Infinity Vision label for existing large-format screens in a bid to compete with Dune’s Imax exclusivity. If Disney’s marketing works, Avengers could draw dollars away from lucrative Dune Imax ticket sales.
Whatever happens with Dune 3, Villeneuve is moving on to Bond next. “I don’t sleep a lot right now because it’s like I have electricity in my veins thinking about this new project,” he told Time. “It is so different. I spent 10 years of my life in the sun talking about a specific color palette, thinking about ways to embrace natural light. I adore being on Arrakis, but I think it’s healthy to step away.”
Photo by Michael Buckner/Variety via Getty Images.
